# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 6. Parent = cand_0003 (current best, val 0.637). cand_0004 and cand_0005 were
BOTH rejected at exactly Δ=-0.077, each breaking ~7 previously-passing tasks and fixing 0.
Scoring: the agent's FINAL code is text-substituted onto two hidden input files (same
layout, different data/rows) and re-run; a task counts only if answer_position matches on
ALL 3. `[0,0,0]` = wrong on the preview too (comprehension or environment/grader fault);
`[1,0,*]` = passes preview, fails a hidden re-run (generalization/boundary gap).

## Method (subagents used)
Fanned out THREE read-only diagnostic subagents over the 36 failing/edge traces (one
group each), extracting per task: instruction, answer_position, final emitted code, score
feedback, test_case_results. Group 1 additionally loaded the actual gold `*_answer.xlsx`
files and diffed our output against them — the strongest evidence. I then verified every
candidate rule directly against the traces before keeping it.

## Diagnosis summary — the residual is a comprehension + grader-fault + boundary ceiling
Three independent passes converged: cand_0001–0003 already harvested every clean
prose-fixable knowledge cluster (RE-RUN/generalization, TYPE/FORMAT, verify-before-finish,
BLANK-vs-ZERO, positional/exact semantics, composite-key, boundary-segment,
run-to-completion). Of the 33 always-failing + a few edge tasks:
- exactly ONE is a genuine, verifiable, SAFE technical gap → **254-34** (fixed this iter);
- several are GRADER/ENVIRONMENT faults (output provably reproduces gold yet scores 0) →
  handed back, NOT optimized against;
- the rest are COMPREHENSION `[0,0,0]` (code generalizes but implements the wrong operation
  on an underspecified spec) or task-specific BOUNDARY `[1,0,*]` with no shared signature —
  neither is safely/verifiably fixable by general prose without the gold answer.

## Ranked issue list (leverage first)
| rank | cluster | tasks (evidence) | root cause | tag | action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Macro/VBA phrased as "write a macro" but graded on cell VALUES | 254-34 `[0,0,0]` (pasted a `Sub HighlightSubsetSums()…End Sub` string into Before!C2; gold = numeric 994110) | Agent treats "write VBA" literally and writes SOURCE TEXT into the answer cell instead of simulating the macro's effect and writing the value | OUTPUT-CONTRACT (additive, narrowing to macro-phrased tasks) | **Edit 1** (prompt.md): macro/VBA/script tasks are graded on resulting cell values; never write source text into a cell — simulate in Python, write the value |
| — | Comprehension / ambiguous-spec `[0,0,0]` | 269-44, 146-49, 157-4, 398-14, 413-15, 577-40, 585-41, 10281, 32468, 39946, 50526, 53449, 55039, 6698, 45944, 55912 | Wrong reading of an underspecified instruction (column order/sort, hyphen-vs-zero, extra sentinel values, total placement, comma removal, state-machine phase, ambiguous match). Code already generalizes. Gold-specific; unverifiable without leaking the answer. | SKIPPED (unverifiable — fails VERIFIED/SAFE) | not edited |
| — | Task-specific BOUNDARY `[1,0,*]` (no shared signature) | 250-20 (exact-duplicate rows deduped vs summed), 42930 (tie-break), 30930/32975 (group-boundary), 49782, 53305, 58890, 58484, 48983 | Passes preview, fails one hidden instance for a data-distribution-specific reason. The boundary/run-segment prose (cand_0002/0003) already covers the general cases; the residue is per-task and can't be narrowed to a safe general rule. | SKIPPED (no shared signature; boundary prose already present) | not edited |
| — | GRADER / ENVIRONMENT faults | 34-5 (our output byte-identical to gold on all 3 yet 0/3), 4225 & 55258 (reproduce the instruction's own stated example yet 0/3), 14207 (harness feedback: "recalculation FAILED … not a prompt defect"), 53062 (formula precedents), 55912 (invalid xlsx) | Infra / grader, not a prompt defect | ENVIRONMENT (handed back) | not worked around |
| — | Volatile current-date | 32023 (TODAY()-relative vs static gold snapshot) | Unknowable reference date | SKIPPED | not edited |

## Change made this iteration (1 edit — ADDITIVE, bounded)
| edit | class | file | what & why it generalizes | blast radius |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | OUTPUT-CONTRACT (missing rule, narrowing) | prompt.md | New bullet after the "prefer literal values" line: when the instruction is phrased as writing a macro/VBA/script, the task is still graded only on the resulting cell VALUES in answer_position; do NOT write macro/VBA/script SOURCE TEXT into a cell — reproduce in Python what the macro would do and write the resulting value(s). States a rule over the whole macro-phrased class; encodes no task id/value/answer. | **BOUNDED** — fires only on macro/VBA/script-phrased tasks. The 10 currently-passing macro tasks (105-24, 139-16, 145-13, 168-17, 353-19, 41-12, 430-43, 494-13, 567-21, 94-28) ALL already simulate the effect and write values — the rule DESCRIBES their existing behavior, so it cannot flip them. 254-34 is the ONLY trace that writes VBA source into a cell; writing source text into a graded cell is never the gold answer, so no passing task relies on the old (absent) behavior. |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes)
- 254-34 (`[0,0,0]`): the trace comment reads "Put a general VBA backtracking solution in
  C2" and `ws["C2"] = answer` where `answer` is a full `Sub … End Sub` string; the gold
  answer cell is the numeric sum `994110`. With Edit 1 present, the agent is told the macro
  phrasing is graded on VALUES and must simulate the macro in Python and write the value —
  directly reversing the exact decision that produced the wrong output. (Full pass also
  needs green-fill detection + summing, which the existing color-detection guidance on
  line 24 already covers; the VBA-source paste was the primary, always-wrong error.)
- SAFE check (behavioral, enumerated): grepped all 91 traces — 18 have macro/VBA/script in
  the instruction; 10 of those pass `[1,1,1]` and every one writes computed VALUES (not
  source); only 254-34 embeds VBA source. So the edit changes behavior on exactly the
  failing case and on none of the passing class.

## Confirmed-SAFE checks I ran
- Placeholders: all six required + {max_turns} intact in task_template.md (untouched this
  iteration). prompt.md contains zero `{`/`}`.
- Edit is ADDITIVE (one new bullet); no existing rule reworded looser, none deleted, no
  global decision/permission rule altered. No task-specific id/value/date/answer encoded.
- Did NOT re-add the refuted "never write formulas / always literals" rule: verified
  directly that 35747, 37962, 45581, 49237, 54675 all WRITE Excel formulas (=IF/=IFERROR/
  =COUNTIFS/=LOOKUP) and all pass `[1,1,1]` → the grader DOES recalc formulas, so a global
  formula ban would regress those 5. (A group-3 subagent proposed this rule; I disproved it
  empirically and dropped it.) Did NOT re-add cand_0004's executed self-test or cand_0005's
  key-canonicalization bullet (both REJECTED).

## Deliberately skipped — and the PLATEAU / CEILING signal (evidence for the handover)
- I shipped ONE fix, not many, because three independent diagnostic passes (one loading the
  gold files) found exactly ONE cluster passing all three tests. Breadth is not available
  this iteration: the remaining failures are comprehension (needs gold → unverifiable),
  grader/environment faults (handed back), or per-task boundary gaps with no shared
  signature. Manufacturing breadth with speculative comprehension prose is precisely what
  sank cand_0004/0005 (both broke ~7 previously-passing tasks, fixed 0).
- STRONG CEILING EVIDENCE: 34-5's output is byte-value-identical to gold on all three
  instances yet scores 0/3 (grader fault); 4225 and 55258 reproduce the instruction's own
  stated example yet score 0/3; 14207's harness feedback explicitly says recalculation
  failed and is "not a prompt defect." These tasks are UNWINNABLE by any prompt change — the
  0.637 champion already includes several tasks the grader will never pass. The two prior
  rejections at identical Δ=-0.077 breaking previously-*fixed* tasks (36478, 47699, 50486,
  56561, 50682, 49237, 31420) indicate an eval noise floor of ~7 tasks and that any edit
  actively CHANGING agent behavior on the general class perturbs these near-boundary tasks.
  I therefore chose the single edit whose behavioral change is confined to a pattern
  (VBA-source-in-cell) that no passing task exhibits.
- Next lever if this does not clear the bar: the residual is the comprehension + grader
  ceiling, which prose cannot safely close without gold. The honest next step is to hand
  back that ceiling with this evidence rather than ship speculative comprehension prose.
